title: MD coarse-graining and acceleration for ion transport in solid-state electrolytes
description: Can we learn an efficient representation or dynamics model from atomistic simulations (MLIP-MD, AIMD) that predicts Li-ion transport (diffusivity, conductivity, hop rates, migration pathways, correlated migration) accurately at larger spatial and temporal scales? Seven method families from classical accelerated MD to generative dynamics, read against that question. Seeded from the review in notes/.

nodes.label: A. Fast MD / learned integrator
nodes.summary: Keeps: the full atomistic description and the physical structure of the dynamics (symplecticity, time reversibility). Discards: the intermediate integration steps, by learning a map over a long time interval. Still computes: MD, with far fewer steps. Open issue: large steps when fast lattice vibrations couple strongly to slow ion migration.

nodes.label: B. Spatial coarse-graining
nodes.summary: Keeps: a reduced set of degrees of freedom (CG particles, or only the mobile ions) and an effective potential, optionally with memory and noise. Discards: the eliminated atoms' explicit motion. Still computes: MD in the coarse-grained space. The eliminated degrees of freedom still act on the kept ones (Mori-Zwanzig), which a potential alone cannot represent.

nodes.label: C. Enhanced sampling
nodes.summary: Keeps: all atoms. Discards: the natural visiting order of states, by adding a bias along collective variables so rare states are reached. Still computes: biased MD, from which rates must be recovered under the method's conditions. Covers metadynamics, OPES, umbrella sampling, weighted ensemble and learned collective variables.

nodes.label: D. Accelerated dynamics
nodes.summary: Keeps: the correct state-to-state dynamics of activated processes. Discards: the time spent waiting in metastable basins, by hyperdynamics, parallel replica or temperature-accelerated dynamics. Still computes: MD with an acceleration strategy. Decades older than the ML approaches and the natural baseline for them.

nodes.label: E. Kinetic coarse-graining
nodes.summary: Keeps: discrete states and the transition probabilities or rates between them (Markov state models, kinetic Monte Carlo, transition path theory). Discards: continuous atomic motion within a state. Still computes: MD only to build the model; afterwards none. Compresses the state space, not the atoms.

nodes.label: F. Generative dynamics / neural simulators
nodes.summary: Keeps: a learned distribution over future states or displacements, or a latent dynamics with a decoder. Discards: step-by-step integration and, in latent variants, explicit atoms between steps. Still computes: MD only for training data; none at inference. Separates into direct displacement models (LiFlow), latent propagators (LSS) and descriptor-space predictors.

nodes.label: G. Adaptive / multiscale simulation
nodes.summary: Keeps: full resolution where and when it matters. Discards: resolution elsewhere, switching representations by region, time or event. Still computes: atomistic MD in part of the system or part of the time. For solid electrolytes an event-driven variant (simplified dynamics in a site, atomistic near a bottleneck) is a proposal, not an existing method.

nodes.label: Action learning (learned long-time-step integrator)
nodes.summary: Learn the mechanical action of a long time interval so the induced map (R_t, V_t) -> (R_{t+dt}, V_{t+dt}) is symplectic and time-reversible by construction.

nodes.label: Force matching
nodes.summary: Fit a coarse-grained potential by minimising the difference between its forces and the atomistic forces projected onto the CG variables; yields the CG free-energy surface.

nodes.label: Coarse-graining auto-encoder
nodes.summary: A variational auto-encoder whose encoder is the CG mapping, trained jointly with a CG force field and a decoder that reconstructs atomistic configurations.

nodes.label: Graph-neural-network CG potential
nodes.summary: A graph neural network over CG beads as the transferable CG interaction model, trained by force matching.

nodes.label: Generalized Langevin / Mori-Zwanzig memory
nodes.summary: CG dynamics with a memory kernel, dissipation and noise derived from the eliminated degrees of freedom (Mori-Zwanzig projection); the many-body form couples the kernels across particles.

nodes.label: Denoising force matching
nodes.summary: Force matching combined with a denoising objective on perturbed configurations, lowering the data needed for a CG model.

nodes.label: Metadynamics
nodes.summary: Enhanced sampling that deposits a history-dependent bias along collective variables to push the system out of visited states.

nodes.label: Infrequent metadynamics (kinetics from biased runs)
nodes.summary: Deposit bias rarely enough that transition states stay unbiased; rescale escape times by the accumulated bias to recover unbiased rates.

nodes.label: State predictive information bottleneck (SPIB)
nodes.summary: Learn a low-dimensional reaction coordinate as the information bottleneck that predicts the future metastable state after a lag time; works from short or under-sampled trajectories.

nodes.label: Weighted ensemble
nodes.summary: Run many unbiased trajectories, split and merge them with weight bookkeeping so rare regions keep walkers; rates follow from the weight flux.

nodes.label: Hyperdynamics
nodes.summary: Add a bias potential that raises metastable basins but vanishes at dividing surfaces; the clock is advanced by the boost factor, preserving the state-to-state sequence.

nodes.label: Parallel replica dynamics
nodes.summary: Run independent replicas of the same state; the first escape in any replica is the next transition, with time summed over replicas.

nodes.label: Temperature-accelerated dynamics
nodes.summary: Run at raised temperature, record escapes, and filter them with harmonic transition-state theory to reproduce the low-temperature sequence of events.

nodes.label: Markov state model
nodes.summary: Discretise configurations into states and estimate the transition matrix P(s_{t+tau} | s_t) at lag tau; implied time scales and populations follow from its spectrum.

nodes.label: Variational approach for Markov processes (VAMP)
nodes.summary: A variational score for the quality of a state decomposition or feature map, used to train deep networks that build Markov state models end to end.

nodes.label: Kinetic Monte Carlo
nodes.summary: Stochastic simulation of transitions from a catalog of events and rates; the clock advances by exponential waiting times.

nodes.label: Kinetic activation-relaxation technique (k-ART)
nodes.summary: Off-lattice, self-learning kinetic Monte Carlo: saddle points are searched from the local environment with the activation-relaxation technique and catalogued by topology, so no predefined lattice event list is needed.

nodes.label: Unsupervised landmark analysis
nodes.summary: Identify sites (landmarks) and ion hops from an MD trajectory without a predefined lattice, by clustering the mobile ions' positions and detecting changes of landmark.

nodes.label: Flow matching
nodes.summary: Train a velocity field that transports a simple reference distribution to the target; here the target is the conditional distribution of atomic displacements.

nodes.label: Latent-space propagator (encoder, propagator, decoder)
nodes.summary: Encode configurations to slow latent variables, learn a stochastic propagator in the latent space over a lag time, and decode back to atomistic configurations.

nodes.label: Descriptor-space trajectory prediction
nodes.summary: Compress the simulation state into atomic-descriptor statistics and predict their time series directly, with an uncertainty estimate.

nodes.label: Boltzmann generator
nodes.summary: A normalizing flow trained to sample the Boltzmann distribution P(R) directly, reweighted to exactness; produces equilibrium configurations without a trajectory.

nodes.label: Adaptive resolution scheme (AdResS)
nodes.summary: Couple atomistic and coarse-grained regions so molecules change resolution on crossing a transition zone, with forces interpolated for momentum conservation.

nodes.label: Radial distribution function
nodes.definition: For a pair of species in a trajectory: the histogram of interatomic distances, normalised by the ideal-gas expectation at the same density.

nodes.label: Site occupancy
nodes.definition: For a set of crystallographic or detected sites: the fraction of frames in which each site holds a mobile ion, averaged over the trajectory.

nodes.label: Free-energy difference
nodes.definition: Between two states or along a collective variable: -kT times the log ratio of their equilibrium populations, estimated from (biased or unbiased) sampling.

nodes.label: Residence time
nodes.definition: For a mobile ion and a site: the mean time between arriving at the site and the next hop away, from hop events detected in the trajectory.

nodes.label: Hop rate
nodes.definition: Number of detected hops of a mobile ion between sites per ion per unit time, from a trajectory or from a rate model; the escape rate in rate-theory terms.

nodes.label: Transition probability
nodes.definition: For discrete states and a lag time tau: the probability of being in state j at t+tau given state i at t, estimated by counting transitions in trajectories.

nodes.label: Mean squared displacement
nodes.definition: For the mobile species: the average over ions and time origins of |r(t0+t) - r(t0)|^2, as a function of lag t.

nodes.label: Diffusivity
nodes.definition: The tracer diffusion coefficient: lim MSD(t) / (2 d t) over the diffusive regime of the MSD, with d the dimension.

nodes.label: Correlation factor
nodes.definition: The ratio of the tracer diffusivity to the diffusivity of an uncorrelated random walk with the same hop rate and jump length; below 1 when successive hops are anticorrelated.

nodes.label: Ionic conductivity
nodes.definition: From the Nernst-Einstein relation with the charge diffusivity (collective displacement of all mobile ions), or from the Green-Kubo current autocorrelation.

nodes.label: Migration pathway
nodes.definition: The sequence of sites and the saddle region a mobile ion passes through in a hop, identified from trajectories or from saddle-point searches; cooperative when several ions move in one event.

nodes.label: Learning the Action for Long-Time-Step Simulations of Molecular Dynamics
nodes.summary: Avoids the energy-conservation and equipartition failures of generic ML trajectory predictors; trains from short trajectories and transfers across temperatures and compositions. Validation levels here follow the review's description (conservation and equipartition); the paper should be checked for any diffusion test.
nodes.learns: A long-time-step map of positions and velocities, through a learned action that enforces symplecticity and time reversibility.
nodes.discards: Nothing in the degrees of freedom; the intermediate integration steps are skipped.

nodes.label: Coarse-graining auto-encoders for molecular dynamics
nodes.summary: The mapping need not be fixed by hand. The CG potential reproduces equilibrium properties; the review flags that this does not give the CG dynamics the correct time scales.
nodes.learns: The CG mapping (encoder), the effective CG force field, and a decoder that reconstructs atomistic configurations, jointly.
nodes.discards: The eliminated atoms' explicit motion; the dynamics of the CG variables are not matched to the atomistic time scales.

nodes.label: Machine learning of coarse-grained molecular dynamics force fields
nodes.summary: The reference neural CG force field; free-energy surfaces of small proteins are reproduced.
nodes.learns: A CG free-energy function (CGnet) by force matching with a neural network and physics-based priors.
nodes.discards: The eliminated atoms; any memory or friction from them.

nodes.label: Coarse graining molecular dynamics with graph neural networks
nodes.summary: Cited in the original review as Olsson et al. 2020 (PMC7671749).
nodes.learns: A transferable CG interaction model as a graph neural network over beads.
nodes.discards: The eliminated atoms; memory and friction.

nodes.label: Construction of coarse-grained molecular dynamics with many-body non-Markovian memory
nodes.summary: Shows that many-body memory is needed to predict collective transport and diffusion correctly; the reason the review doubts that a Li-only CG potential can predict diffusion kinetics in solid electrolytes.
nodes.learns: A CG model with a many-body, non-Markovian memory kernel in addition to the effective potential.
nodes.discards: The eliminated degrees of freedom, but their effect is kept as memory and noise rather than dropped.

nodes.label: Force matching with denoising for data-efficient coarse-grained models
nodes.summary: Lowers the data requirement of CG models substantially.
nodes.learns: A CG potential from force matching plus a denoising objective, with far fewer atomistic samples.
nodes.discards: The eliminated atoms; memory and friction.

nodes.label: From metadynamics to dynamics
nodes.summary: The standard route from biased sampling back to kinetics, with its applicability conditions.
nodes.learns: Unbiased transition rates from metadynamics runs with infrequent bias deposition.
nodes.discards: The natural visiting order; recovers time only under the condition that transition states stay unbiased.

nodes.label: State predictive information bottleneck
nodes.summary: Learns the slow coordinate that predicts the future metastable state; feeds enhanced sampling.
nodes.learns: A reaction coordinate from time-lagged (dynamical) information, including from under-sampled trajectories.
nodes.discards: Fast degrees of freedom orthogonal to the learned coordinate.

nodes.label: Enhanced sampling with machine-learning-based collective variables (SPIB-guided metadynamics)
nodes.summary: Closes the loop between CV learning and enhanced sampling.
nodes.venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
nodes.learns: Collective variables (SPIB) that are then used to bias metadynamics, iterated.
nodes.discards: The natural visiting order of states.

nodes.label: Weighted ensemble simulation: review of methodology, applications, and software
nodes.summary: Rates follow from unbiased weight flux, so no bias correction is needed.
nodes.learns: Nothing (a review); describes weight-splitting schemes that sample rare events without biasing the dynamics.
nodes.discards: Nothing in the dynamics; compute is redistributed among trajectories.

nodes.label: Hyperdynamics: accelerated molecular dynamics of infrequent events
nodes.summary: Correct state-to-state dynamics with a rigorous time rescaling, under transition-state-theory assumptions.
nodes.learns: Nothing is learned; a bias potential that vanishes on dividing surfaces accelerates escapes with a known boost factor.
nodes.discards: The waiting time inside basins.

nodes.label: Extending the time scale in atomistic simulation of materials
nodes.summary: The theoretical reference and baseline for ML accelerators; the review keeps it as the standard against which learned methods are judged.
nodes.learns: Nothing (a review) of hyperdynamics, parallel replica dynamics, temperature-accelerated dynamics and on-the-fly kMC.
nodes.discards: The waiting time in basins, by each method's own device.

nodes.label: VAMPnets for deep learning of molecular kinetics
nodes.summary: Deep Markov state models without hand-built features.
nodes.learns: A state decomposition and transition matrix end to end, by maximising the VAMP score.
nodes.discards: Continuous motion within states; a lag time is chosen.

nodes.label: Unsupervised landmark analysis for jump detection in molecular dynamics simulations
nodes.summary: Already read by the researcher. Solves trajectory analysis, not prediction. Published version in Physical Review Materials: add the DOI from the journal page.
nodes.learns: Sites and hop events from ionic MD trajectories, without a predefined lattice.
nodes.discards: Continuous motion within a site; nothing predictive about new environments.

nodes.label: Kinetic activation-relaxation technique: an off-lattice self-learning kinetic Monte Carlo algorithm
nodes.summary: Handles local distortion and off-lattice motion without a complete predefined event list.
nodes.learns: An event catalog and barriers discovered from local environments during the simulation.
nodes.discards: Continuous motion within basins; requires the local topology classification to hold.

nodes.label: Molecular latent space simulators
nodes.summary: Generates long trajectories of protein models at far lower cost than MD, reproducing the slow kinetics.
nodes.learns: Slow latent variables, a stochastic propagator in that space, and a decoder to atomistic configurations.
nodes.discards: Fast motion orthogonal to the slow variables; explicit atoms between decoded frames.

nodes.label: Compression and prediction of materials simulation trajectories with atomic descriptors
nodes.summary: A third route beside direct displacement models and latent propagators.
nodes.learns: A compressed state built from atomic descriptors and its time series, with uncertainty.
nodes.discards: Atomic positions; only descriptor statistics are propagated.

nodes.label: Flow matching for accelerated simulation of atomic transport in crystalline materials (LiFlow)
nodes.summary: Trained on 25 ps MD trajectories of 4,186 solid-electrolyte candidates at several temperatures. Li MSD on unseen compositions: Spearman about 0.7 to 0.8. Reported speed-up up to about 600,000x relative to AIMD. The paper closest to the researcher's problem.
nodes.learns: P(dR | R_t, T): the distribution of atomic displacements over a time interval given the current structure and temperature; a Propagator generates them and a Corrector repairs unphysical structures.
nodes.discards: Step-by-step integration; the model is conditioned on structure and temperature only and still needs MD trajectories to train.

nodes.label: Boltzmann generators: sampling equilibrium states of many-body systems with deep learning
nodes.summary: Equilibrium structures and free energies without MD; a different objective from any dynamics model.
nodes.learns: A normalizing flow from a simple prior to the Boltzmann distribution, reweighted to exactness.
nodes.discards: Time altogether: no trajectory and no transition dynamics.

nodes.label: Adaptive resolution molecular-dynamics simulation: changing the degrees of freedom on the fly
nodes.summary: The review proposes an event-driven analogue for solid electrolytes; AdResS itself has not done this.
nodes.learns: Nothing is learned; molecules switch between atomistic and CG representations by region.
nodes.discards: Atomistic detail in the coarse region, with momentum-conserving coupling across the transition zone.

nodes.label: A CG potential that reproduces the equilibrium distribution does not determine the time scales of the CG dynamics
nodes.summary: The eliminated degrees of freedom act on the kept ones through dissipation, noise and memory (Mori-Zwanzig); matching P(R) leaves these unconstrained, so diffusion and collective transport can be wrong even when structure and free energies are right.
nodes.scope: Coarse-grained models of any kind; acute for Li-only models of solid electrolytes.

nodes.label: Coarse-graining away the host lattice leaves its effect on the mobile ions, which must be represented as friction, noise or memory
nodes.summary: The reviewer's inference from the Mori-Zwanzig argument applied to solid electrolytes: a Li-only CG particle model with a simple effective potential is unlikely to predict diffusion kinetics.

nodes.label: The coarse-grained mapping can be learned jointly with the CG potential rather than fixed by hand
nodes.summary: An encoder trained with the CG force field and a decoder yields a mapping and a potential together.

nodes.label: Sampling more transition events does not by itself give correct transition rates
nodes.summary: Biased sampling changes the dynamics; rates are recovered only under the method's conditions (e.g. infrequent bias deposition with unbiased transition states), or by schemes that never bias the dynamics (weighted ensemble).

nodes.label: In activated diffusion the time spent waiting in basins far exceeds the transition time, so skipping the waiting gives large speed-ups while keeping the state-to-state dynamics
nodes.summary: The premise of hyperdynamics, parallel replica and temperature-accelerated dynamics, with rigorous time rescaling under transition-state-theory assumptions.

nodes.label: A symplectic, time-reversible long-time-step map need not reproduce long-time diffusion statistics
nodes.summary: The reviewer's caution on learned integrators: geometric structure prevents energy drift and equipartition failure but does not by itself constrain diffusivity or rare-event rates.

nodes.label: A model of the equilibrium distribution P(R) does not predict transitions P(R_{t+tau} | R_t), so equilibrium generators cannot give diffusion coefficients
nodes.summary: Definitional, but worth a node because much generative molecular simulation targets equilibrium sampling rather than time evolution.

nodes.label: Agreement in MSD does not establish correct migration mechanisms, transition rates or correlated motion
nodes.summary: The central question about LiFlow and generative dynamics in general: whether a model that reproduces MSD also reproduces pathways, hop rates and cooperative hopping. No evidence either way in the reviewed papers.
nodes.scope: Generative dynamics models of ion transport.

nodes.label: LiFlow's reported speed-up (about 600,000x) is relative to ab initio MD, not to GPU-accelerated MLIP-MD
nodes.summary: The comparison in the paper is against first-principles simulation; the speed-up over an MLIP-MD baseline would be far smaller and is not reported.

nodes.label: Effective dynamics cannot be learned from short MD trajectories alone when important migration pathways never appear in them
nodes.summary: If a pathway is absent from training data the model cannot identify it; enhanced sampling, active exploration or physical constraints may be required. Not tested in the reviewed papers.
nodes.scope: Learned dynamics models trained on short trajectories.

nodes.label: Which degrees of freedom coarse-graining should eliminate for solid electrolytes is undetermined
nodes.summary: Candidates lose different information: high-frequency lattice vibrations (keeping coordinates); framework atoms (keeping ions and an effective environment); in-site vibrations (keeping occupancy and events); or all explicit structure (continuous latent dynamics).

nodes.label: Structural and MSD agreement can coexist with wrong migration pathways, so validation must be layered by research goal
nodes.summary: The reviewer's position: check structural, thermodynamic, kinetic, transport and mechanistic levels separately; a model with poor instantaneous positions but correct transition kinetics may still suit long-time transport.

nodes.label: Automatic site and hop detection from trajectories is analysis, not a predictive kinetic model for new environments
nodes.summary: Landmark analysis extracts sites and hops from existing trajectories; a model that predicts kinetics in unseen structures is a further step.

nodes.label: An event-driven multiscale scheme (simplified dynamics while an ion sits in a site, atomistic MLIP near a bottleneck) would suit solid electrolytes
nodes.summary: The reviewer's proposal by analogy with adaptive resolution; not implemented in the reviewed literature.

edges.label: integrator structure vs learned distribution
edges.note: Both learn atomic motion over long intervals; A keeps the geometric structure of the dynamics, F learns the transition distribution directly.

edges.label: biased sampling vs skipped waiting
edges.note: Both accelerate rare events; the conditions under which true time and dynamics are recovered differ.

edges.label: fewer atoms vs fewer states
edges.note: B compresses atomic degrees of freedom; E compresses the state space.

edges.label: explicit rates vs learned distributions
edges.note: Both replace step-by-step MD; E has explicit states, transitions and rates, F learns continuous or discrete distributions.

edges.label: adds memory, dissipation and noise to the CG potential
explicit slow-variable dynamics vs direct displacement distribution
edges.note: LSS builds an explicit low-dimensional dynamics first; flow matching (LiFlow) learns the displacement distribution without one.

edges.label: samples P(R) vs learns P(dR | R_t, T)
tracer diffusivity over the random-walk value
random-walk reference uses the hop rate
adds many-body memory
edges.note: Memory corrects the dynamics that a force-matched CG potential alone gets wrong.

edges.label: uses SPIB coordinates to bias metadynamics
explicit latent slow-variable model vs direct displacement distribution
automatic event discovery: analysis vs simulation
